prompt: Read the rahul-bangre/machine-slop repo on GitHub to understand what it does, then read E2B's docs. Open an issue on the repo listing the 3 most important things E2B can do that machine-slop can't yet, with a link to the E2B docs for each.

intent: Open the machine-slop repo to understand what it does.

title: GitHub - rahul-bangre/machine-slop: give agents disposable computers on your machine · GitHub

intent: Read the machines crate docs to learn existing features.
Read agentd docs to see file, process and port features.
Open E2B docs to see their feature list.
Open the docs index to find exact feature page links.
Write the issue body and post it to GitHub.
command:
cat > issue.json <<'EOF'
{
  "title": "Gaps vs E2B: custom templates, persistent volumes, stateful code interpreter",
  "body": "machine-slop already covers much of what E2B does: pause/resume with memory, fork, snapshots, idempotent creates, egress allowlists, credential-injecting egress, public previews and tenants. After comparing the READMEs with the E2B docs, these look like the three most important gaps.

### 1. Custom templates
Every machine boots from one shared read-only rootfs image (curl, git, Node, Python, Chromium). E2B lets users define their own environment with a base image, files, packages and start/ready commands. They build it once, version it with tags, and start sandboxes from it. In machine-slop today the only way to get a custom environment is to set up a machine and snapshot it.
- Docs: https://docs.e2b.dev/template/quickstart

### 2. Persistent volumes
A machine's writes go to its own scratch disk and are removed when it is destroyed. E2B volumes are storage that exists apart from any sandbox. They can be mounted into several sandboxes at custom paths and read or written through the SDK.
- Docs: https://docs.e2b.dev/volumes

### 3. Stateful code interpreter
agentd runs processes, but no runtime keeps state between calls. E2B's Code Interpreter offers `runCode()` with persistent contexts that keep variables between calls. It supports multiple languages (Python, JS/TS, R, Java, bash) and returns rich results like charts. Most LLM tool-use integrations expect this.
- Docs: https://docs.e2b.dev/code-interpreting/contexts
- Charts: https://docs.e2b.dev/code-interpreting/create-charts-visualizations"
}
EOF
curl -sS -X POST -H 'Accept: application/vnd.github+json' --data @issue.json https://api.github.com/repos/rahul-bangre/machine-slop/issues | grep -E '"(html_url|number|message)"' | head

intent: Issue created; report the link and finish.
summary: I opened issue #28 (https://github.com/rahul-bangre/machine-slop/issues/28), which lists three things E2B can do that machine-slop can't yet, each with an E2B docs link: building custom environment templates, storage volumes that persist apart from any machine, and a code interpreter that keeps variables between calls and returns charts. I left out features machine-slop already has, like pause/resume, fork, snapshots, network allowlists and public previews; I didn't check the repo's one existing open issue for overlap.
